Title: Finite State Raises $27 Million to Secure Software and Firmware in Connected Devices
Context: The platform identifies both known and zero-day vulnerabilities and helps manufacturers fix the ones that can be exploited
Full Text:
Product security firm Finite State announced on Tuesday that it raised $27 million in a Series C funding round to grow its international presence and make its connected device security platform more autonomous.

Private funds managed by The O.H.I.O. Fund led the round, with participation from CIBC Innovation Banking, Energy Impact Partners, Energize Capital, and National Grid Partners.

The company tied the investment to two pressures on manufacturers. One is a wave of critical flaws uncovered by AI-powered research in October, dubbed the ‘Vulnpocalypse’, and the other is a growing set of product security mandates.

Finite State’s platform inspects the code that actually ships in a device, covering both software and firmware. It works from compiled firmware and binaries, so source code is not required.

Its users are makers of vehicles, medical devices, industrial equipment, consumer electronics and utility infrastructure. The platform identifies both known and zero-day vulnerabilities and helps manufacturers fix the ones that can be exploited.

On the compliance side, the platform continuously produces SBOMs, VEX documents and signed compliance packages to help device makers meet regulations such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). The company also cites FDA premarket cybersecurity requirements, the UNECE R155 and R156 vehicle regulations, and the IEC 62443 industrial standard among the rules manufacturers face.

AI agents carry out analysis, triage and testing on the platform and draft regulatory reports. Customers can also connect their own agents through an API and an MCP server.

Finite State delivers the evidence, intelligence, and automation to protect manufacturers, organizations, and consumers.”

Title: Bay Raises $50 Million to Control What Enterprise AI Agents Can Do
Context: Bay was founded in February 2026 by Yuval Zacharia (CEO), Boris Danilovich (VP of R&D), and Aner Morag (CPO)
Full Text:
Tel Aviv-based Bay has emerged from stealth with $50 million funding (comprising a $37 million Series A round led by Battery Ventures and a previously undisclosed $13 million seed funding led by YL Ventures and Striker Venture Partners). Bay was founded in February 2026 by Yuval Zacharia (CEO), Boris Danilovich (VP of R&D), and Aner Morag (CPO). All three are alumni of the Israeli Military Intelligence (IDF Unit 8200).

In business, companies cannot ignore the economic advantage offered by AI agents, but nor do they always know what any individual agent might do. Agentic AI behavior is decided at runtime by each agent acting on its user’s behalf and with its user’s permissions.

Bay is designed to allow companies to install and employ AI agents confident that they will not run amok with unintended actions. It provides a single control plane that discovers, understands and controls agents wherever they run.

When installed, Bay automatically builds a full inventory of the AI agents, coding assistants, MCP servers, skills, extensions and local models in use, and maps how they connect, including risky combinations of tools. It follows each agent session from the first prompt to the final action. Its Enforcer component evaluates every proposed action in the context of the full session and decides in milliseconds whether to allow the action, refer it to the user, redirect it based on policy, or simply deny it.

The policy guiding Enforcer’s actions is automatically built and maintained by Bay’s embedded AI system (Lighthouse) based on the organization’s own activity history.

By focusing on the agents’ actions, Bay protects against dangerous agent activity regardless of whether the cause is malicious human-directed prompt injection or organic agent purpose drift.

“Before we even decided what to build, we agreed on three non-negotiables,” Bay’s CEO and co-founder Yuval Zacharia told SecurityWeek: “effortless deployment, immediate time to value, and a clear path to operationalization.”

These principles became the design foundation for Bay. “The first drove us to build a flexible, agentless architecture that can be deployed across an entire fleet in under five minutes,” she continued. “The second led to patented technology that retrospectively analyzes 30 days of historical logs, allowing customers to see what Bay would have delivered had it been running in their environment. This makes it possible to demonstrate business value almost immediately and complete a proof of value in less than 14 days.”

The third, she concluded, “shaped how we approach day-to-day operations, with clear ownership, AI-driven policy creation, and a product designed to become part of how teams actually work.”

The funding will be used to further develop the product and expand the firm’s engineering team, and to invest in go-to-market plans across the US and Europe, “Longer term,” explains the firm, “we want Bay to be the core control layer for enterprises putting AI agents to work at scale. As agents take on longer-running, more autonomous work, Bay’s job is to make sure organizations can trust them with it, and to keep expanding what agents can safely do on their own.”

Title: Dreeze Emerges From Stealth With $33M to Rebuild Cloud Apps After Cyberattacks
Context: Cloud application recovery startup Dreeze announced on Tuesday that it raised $33 million in a seed funding round as it emerged from stealth mode with a platform built to bring...
Full Text:
Cloud application recovery startup Dreeze announced on Tuesday that it raised $33 million in a seed funding round as it emerged from stealth mode with a platform built to bring back whole cloud applications instead of only the data behind them.

The round was led by Norwest and Bessemer Venture Partners, with Claltech also investing.

Dreeze, whose staff is split between Israel and the United States, said the money will go toward product development, bigger sales and marketing teams, and getting its platform into more enterprises.

The company was formed in 2025 by Avi Raichel and brothers Ziv and Oded Kedem. The three previously worked together at Zerto, which HPE acquired, and Kashya.

Dreeze’s argument is that getting data back after an incident is not the same as getting an application running again. A cyberattack or a mistake by an AI agent can leave an organization with its data intact but without the configurations, secrets, infrastructure and connections the application needs.

Its platform, named Application Revival, scans the customer’s cloud environment on an ongoing basis, works out which resources and dependencies belong to which application, and generates a recovery plan from the live environment. Backups of data and configurations are stored with those recovery plans in an immutable, isolated vault under the customer’s control.

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

In a recovery scenario, Application Revival automatically reconstructs the application as a whole. Customers can also run recovery tests in an isolated account, with no impact on production.

“Companies have spent years getting better at backing up data, but getting the data back doesn’t mean the business is back,” said Ziv Kedem, the company’s CEO. “With cyber threats increasing and AI introducing new risks, enterprises need to assume that critical applications will go down.”

“We started Dreeze because recovery needs to go further. Our goal is to make Application Revival the new standard, so companies know they have a proven path to bring their applications back when something goes wrong,” he added.

The AWS version of the platform is generally available. Support for Microsoft Azure is in early access, with general availability expected in early 2027.

Full Text:
Funding Will Scale Finite State’s Autonomous Platform and International Expansion as Manufacturers Face a Surge of AI-Discovered Flaws and New Global Security Mandates

Finite State, a leader in product security and software supply chain risk management, today announced a $27 million Series C funding round led by private funds managed by The O.H.I.O. Fund, with participation from CIBC Innovation Banking, Energy Impact Partners, Energize Capital, and National Grid Partners to continue its mission to secure the world’s connected devices.

Finite State’s AI-driven product security platform analyzes the software and firmware inside finished devices, giving manufacturers visibility into the products they build and sell, from vehicles and medical devices to industrial equipment, consumer electronics and critical utility infrastructure. The platform uncovers both known and zero-day vulnerabilities and guides manufacturers in fixing the exploitable ones before attackers strike, making everyday life safer and more secure.

The new capital will expand Finite State’s already global operations, deepen its presence across key international markets, and accelerate development of the platform’s autonomous capabilities. These investments will enable more manufacturers around the world to uncover the gap between the software they plan to ship and what actually runs in the finished device, and to continuously identify and mitigate security risks across increasingly complex software supply chains.

The funding comes at a turning point for product security. In October, AI-powered research uncovered critical flaws in some of the world’s most widely used software, including a vulnerability in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the web, in a surge security leaders have dubbed the “Vulnpocalypse.” AI has shrunk the time it takes to find a flaw and turn it into an attack from weeks to days, and sometimes hours. Connected devices are especially exposed: a single flaw in a shared open-source component can sit inside millions of shipped products that are hard to inventory and slow to patch. For manufacturers, the urgent question is no longer whether a vulnerability exists. It is which of their products contain it.

In parallel, regulators worldwide now expect connected products to be secure by design, with security built in and demonstrated before a device ships rather than added after it reaches the market. The EU Cyber Resilience Act, FDA premarket cybersecurity requirements, UNECE R155 and R156 for vehicles, and IEC 62443 for industrial systems all place the burden of proof on the manufacturer, and the cost of falling short includes blocked market access, recalls, and liability.

Meeting that standard is difficult because modern connected products are assembled, not written from scratch. A single device can contain open source libraries, third-party components, and legacy code from many suppliers, and what ships in the finished firmware often differs from what the source code and bill of materials describe. Manufacturers cannot secure what they cannot see.

“Every connected product—cars, infusion pumps, toys, OT, baby monitors, your home router—runs on third-party code and components, making inspection and security exceptionally challenging,” said Mike Venerable, Founding Partner, The O.H.I.O. Fund. “Governments worldwide are imposing new regulatory pressures on manufacturers, recognizing how quickly AI-enabled attackers can exploit vulnerabilities. Finite State is solving an incredibly difficult product and technology security challenge by deploying a platform that has earned the trust of investors and customers. We are delighted to support Finite State through this financing and believe the company will be an important solution for connected device security and supply chain risk mitigation.”“Moments like this separate the companies built for what’s coming from those still catching up,” said Brittany Blanco, Innovation Banking Director II, CIBC Innovation Banking. “We’re excited to back a team that saw this shift early and is ready to meet it on a global scale.”

Finite State customers span the world’s critical infrastructure and connected device ecosystem—from national power grids and a U.S. national security research laboratory to global automakers, life-saving medical devices, and the connected hardware running inside homes, hospitals, and factories worldwide. With the IoT security market projected to reach $80.3 billion by 2031,[1] Finite State’s growing international customer base reflects a challenge that increasingly transcends borders: manufacturers must understand exactly what software is inside their products, whether it can be exploited, and what they need to do about it.

Bruce Lin, Senior Manager, Software Department at JET OPTOELECTRONICS CO., LTD., a Tier 1 supplier of automotive electronics and smart cockpit solutions serving global automakers, said: “The depth of Finite State’s binary and firmware analysis, the insight it yields into what’s in a shipped device and not just the build manifest, the direct and transitive dependency visibility, and audit-ready compliance mapped to the regulations we actually face, are all invaluable.”Finite State founder and CEO Matt Wyckhouse said: “The Vulnpocalypse isn’t a one-month event. It’s the new baseline. AI-equipped attackers can now find a flaw faster than most manufacturers can figure out which of their products contain it. Governments are rightly advancing regulations to protect the public good, leaving security teams to prove that risks they identify are understood and addressed. Finite State delivers the evidence, intelligence, and automation to protect manufacturers, organizations, and consumers. This Series C round will enable our talented team to both drive the next generation of remarkable platform advances and expand our global reach to safeguard both our customers and theirs.”

Among its latest honors, Finite State was named to the 2026 Inc. 5000, an annual ranking of the fastest-growing private companies in America, and chosen as a finalist in SiliconANGLE’s prestigious 2026 TechForward Awards in the Security category.

Title: Snyk Named a Leader in The Forrester Wave™: Agentic Development Security Tools, Q4 2026
Context: AI makes it cheap to chain several of those minor issues into a critical exploit path, so the backlog now functions as an attack surface rather than deferred cleanup
Full Text:
We're proud to share that Snyk has been named a Leader in The Forrester Wave™: Agentic Development Security Tools, Q4 2026. Snyk received the highest score in the Strategy category, along with the highest scores possible in these criteria:

Strategy: Vision, Roadmap, and Partner Ecosystem

Current offering: AI dynamic testing, AI coding guardrails, autonomous proprietary code remediation, and developer experience

Software development changed who does the work

For two decades, software development moved at a human pace where developers wrote code, peers reviewed it, and security teams tested it on a schedule. AI coding assistants compressed that cycle, and coding agents are now changing who does the work. Forrester frames the shift: "AI coding agents are changing how software is built, moving from developer assistants to active participants in development workflows."

Adoption has moved well past the pilot stage. In the Stack Overflow 2026 Developer Survey, 66% of developers who use AI work in coding agents, and 73% of those using AI coding assistants or agents use them daily. As a result, the developer's role is shifting from writing every line to orchestrating the agents that write it.

Each of those agents brings its own supply chain; it installs packages, connects to MCP servers, loads skills, and invokes tools the security team may never have reviewed. Because it can also run commands, edit files, and access sensitive data, its actions need to be governed as much as its code needs to be tested. In our view, security models built to scan code after it is written were not designed to govern the systems creating it.

Attackers are moving at machine speed too

In 2025, Anthropic's threat intelligence team disrupted an espionage campaign in which AI carried out an estimated 80 to 90% of tactical operations, with humans in a supervisory role. The CrowdStrike 2026 Global Threat Report puts average eCrime breakout time, from initial access to lateral movement, at 29 minutes, with the fastest observed case at 27 seconds.

Those timelines change how teams should think about their vulnerability backlog. Pull request queues, ticket triage, and quarterly pentests were designed around attackers who moved slower than the fix. Most backlogs consist of low- and medium-severity findings, deprioritized one at a time. AI makes it cheap to chain several of those minor issues into a critical exploit path, so the backlog now functions as an attack surface rather than deferred cleanup.

The pressure is also building inside the codebase; Snyk’s product data shows new critical and high-severity issues detected grew 10x in the past year, and roughly eight new issues are introduced for every one remediated. When risk is created faster than it is fixed, the answer is a different operating model: security agents that fix continuously, guardrails inside the agent workflow, and adversarial testing that proves controls hold

AI applications are reaching production faster than governance

Teams are shipping AI applications and agents into production faster than governance processes can keep pace with. Many security leaders are still working to answer basic questions about their AI estate:

Which models, agents, and MCP servers are running, and what data can they reach?

Which skills were pulled from public registries, and who approved them?

Could you audit what a given agent did last week?

This is shadow AI at enterprise scale. Its risks, such as prompt injection, excessive agency, and data leakage, are behavioral: they live in an agent’s decisions as well as its code, which is why code scanning alone can’t surface them. Model choice is part of that risk. In Snyk’s 2026 State of Agentic AI Adoption, Volume III, the lowest-capability models averaged 501 on decision override, a 0 to 1,000 score, while the most capable models averaged 45, a gap of more than 10x. Roughly a third of the scored model references in US environments fall in that lowest group. Governing them starts with a live inventory of the AI estate, including which models are in play, and policies that apply before an agent acts.

Why this evaluation matters

In our view, Forrester's evaluation reflects these shifts in operating model, and it assessed agentic development security across the full span of AI-driven development: the code agents produce, the agents and the components they pull in, and the AI applications teams build. Forrester asks buyers to weigh three considerations:

Visibility and governance of agentic development

Verification of AI-generated code and AI applications

AI risk reduction at agentic speed

Teams now need coverage across all three, on one platform that shares context between them, and that is the standard we have been building toward.

A decade of conviction, pointed at where software is created now

Snyk has operated on a core belief for more than a decade: security belongs where software is created. We believe agentic development moves that point of creation inside the agent workflow, and that is where the Snyk AI Security Platform is built to operate. Forrester’s report states that "Snyk articulates a farsighted vision to secure AI-written code, the agents that run it, and the applications they build, while advancing secure-at-inception development and governance."

On capabilities, the report states that "Snyk brings security into developer and AI coding agent workflows through autofix and coding guardrails that secure AI- and human-generated code and block risky agent actions." It also notes that Snyk's "strong AI dynamic testing uncovers business logic flaws and vulnerability chains and validates findings with working exploits."

How Evo by Snyk secures each layer of AI-driven development

Last year, Snyk expanded the Snyk AI Security Platform with Evo by Snyk, a suite of agent-native security solutions that secure, protect, and govern AI-driven development across three loops: the code artifact, the AI workforce, and the AI applications teams build. A validation layer tests all three.

Evo Agentic AppSec: Secure the code artifact. AI security agents that find, fix, and block vulnerabilities at the speed agents write code, with every result verified independently. This includes Snyk Secrets for blocking leaked credentials.

Evo Agentic Development Security (ADS): Protect the AI workforce. Governs what AI coding agents use, what they do, and what they generate, from the MCP servers and skills they pull in to the code they write. This includes Snyk Studio for real-time guidance in AI coding workflows.

Evo AI-SPM: Govern every AI app you build. Discovers and assesses risk of the models, agents, skills, and MCP servers in your software, generates a live AI-BOM, and turns AI policy into enforceable controls.

Evo Continuous Offensive Security (COS): Validate every loop. Continuously tests applications and AI agents, leveraging Agent Red Teaming, and returns validated proof of what an attacker could actually exploit, so no loop grades its own work.

As AI takes on more of the work of building software, we believe its output needs a separate, deterministic layer to verify it. That is why Snyk pairs frontier AI reasoning with our deterministic engines and ten years of security intelligence, so organizations can adopt AI at full speed and stay accountable for what they ship.

What this means for teams building with AI agents

Forrester's take: "Snyk is a good fit for enterprises that want to accelerate agentic development while embedding security directly into agent workflows." For teams evaluating this market, three questions help separate tools built for agentic development from tools adapted to it:

Governance: Can you see and control what your agents use, what they do, and what they generate before it ships?

Remediation: Is your fix rate keeping pace with your rate of new risk, across new code and the existing backlog?

Proof: What independent evidence shows your controls hold against a real attacker?

We are grateful to our customers, partners, and the developer community, whose feedback shapes the platform every day. We will keep investing inside the agent loop, where software is now created. Our mission remains the same: unleash AI innovators, securely.

Title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Dreadnode to Bring Automated AI Security Testing to the Falcon Platform
Context: Modern businesses deploy AI models and agents before confirming they’re secure, an approach that can have severe consequences
Full Text:
Today, at Fal.Con EU 2026, I’m excited to share CrowdStrike’s intent to acquire Dreadnode. This acquisition will bring automated AI security testing to the CrowdStrike Falcon® platform so our customers can validate the security of AI systems before they go into production.

Modern businesses deploy AI models and agents before confirming they’re secure, an approach that can have severe consequences. When an agent ships with a weakness that allows jailbreaking or manipulation, it provides the adversary with an opportunity to reach the sensitive systems and data the agent can access. These weaknesses must be discovered before the agent goes into production. Security testing built for conventional software does not find them.

Dreadnode does. Its technology tests AI models, applications, and agents with known attack techniques to learn where they break so fixes can be applied before deployment. CrowdStrike, together with Dreadnode, will extend the Falcon platform into the layer where businesses build AI so every customer can evaluate their AI agents for security gaps and deploy them with confidence.

Dreadnode will be generally available in Q4 FY27. Let’s take a closer look at what it will bring.

Automated AI Security Testing on the Falcon Platform

The probabilistic and dynamic nature of AI agents and LLMs has broken the traditional security testing model, which has long been used to assess code that consistently behaves in the same way. This testing approach can’t identify weaknesses inside the reasoning loop built into AI models and agents.

AI has also introduced new security risks: Prompt injection, jailbreaking, and agent tool manipulation can lead to customer data loss, financial loss, and brand reputation damage. Dreadnode was built to understand the risks to AI systems by probing for vulnerabilities to uncover these issues before adversaries can.

How Dreadnode Works

Users first describe what they want to test in plain language. Dreadnode runs more than 50 attack techniques — including jailbreaks, prompt injection, and multi-turn and agent-specific attacks — against the AI systems, models, model repositories, applications, agents, and MCP servers the business relies on before they reach production.

With the testing complete, Dreadnode ranks findings by severity and maps them to the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, OWASP Agentic Security (ASI01-ASI10), MITRE ATLAS™, and NIST AI RMF. All assessments are aggregated into a single risk picture that includes total findings, attack success rates, severity breakdown, finding outcomes, and deep risk metrics. Dreadnode also delivers an exportable report so stakeholders can make go/no-go decisions.

Key to this process is human-in-the-loop review. Model builders can expand any findings to see the exact attacker prompt and target response, and walk through attacks step-by-step. Operators can reclassify their findings, adjust attack severity levels, and document reasoning. All dashboard metrics will recompute automatically when findings are reclassified.

These findings will fortify CrowdStrike Falcon® Guardian, our flagship AI detection and response (AIDR) solution, which protects enterprise-developed AI at runtime. Dreadnode results will feed into Falcon Guardian as policy recommendations, so a weakness found in testing informs runtime protection. Dreadnode testing data will also strengthen CrowdStrike’s SafeMind models, advancing our research into securing AI systems.

See it in action:

Stronger Security for Enterprise-Developed AI

Businesses are integrating AI models, agents, and applications into daily operations faster than security teams can validate them. Traditional software security testing isn’t built to capture the risks these technologies can present. With Dreadnode, CrowdStrike will extend the Falcon platform to give enterprises a fast, repeatable way to test their AI systems before they’re deployed.

CrowdStrike’s mission has always been to stop breaches. As new technologies emerge and the threat landscape evolves, we must adapt to provide our customers with the robust defense they need. Today, that means delivering solutions that secure AI end-to-end, from development to deployment to runtime. Last year, we acquired Pangea to secure enterprise AI use and development. Last month, we announced Falcon Guardian to deliver runtime protection for AI agents, introduce a new AI gateway, and extend our elite security services to AI systems.

The acquisition of Dreadnode and its automated AI security testing will be a critical step on our journey to protect businesses in the AI era. We are eager to welcome the Dreadnode team.

These statements involve risks and uncertainties, and actual results may differ materially. There are a number of risks that could cause actual results to differ materially, including the satisfaction of the acquisition’s closing conditions, our ability to integrate Dreadnode, and other risks described in the filings we make with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission from time to time.

Ransomware attacks are now a leading cybersecurity threat, with many pointing to the rise of crypto as an enabler. But crypto isn’t the only factor behind the rise of the ransomware market. Full Text:
For the fifth consecutive year, Bitdefender is included as a Representative Vendor in the 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response.

The Market Guide offers a timely opportunity to look beyond the table stakes of 24x7 alert monitoring and understand how modern MDR should leverage AI, how providers should help contain attacks, and the importance of MDR in reducing risk exposure.

As AI-enabled attacks become faster and more frequent, exposure reduction is a critical addition to detection and response.

What Do We Feel Inclusion In the 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response Means?

Gartner says that more than 600 providers offer MDR services. The 30 vendors listed in the Market Guide meet the Gartner combined criteria for inclusion. Representative vendors:

Are consistently visible to Gartner clients (based on inquiries in the prior 18 months and through Gartner Peer Insights reviews from the prior 12 months)

Are variable in size and distribution to reflect the buying population

Have a clear end-user and outcome-focused offering distinct from pure technology-driven offerings

What Are Top Questions to Ask an MDR Vendor?

We believe three practical questions can help uncover whether a service is built around meaningful results.

How does the MDR vendor combine AI with human expertise to investigate threats and guide response decisions?

What actions will the MDR provider take automatically to contain an attack?

How will the MDR team help to identify weaknesses and reduce future risk?

We’ll look at these questions in detail below. They clarify whether a provider can help contain threats, reduce exposure, and support informed response decisions or if they primarily collect and escalate alerts.

MDR marketing claims can be challenging to sort out. According to Gartner: “Buyers continue to face challenges with service naming and marketing language that has often overpromised and underdelivered, adding confusion rather than clarity.”

What Is AI’s Optimal Role in MDR?

We believe AI should help security teams move faster, while people and threat intelligence guide investigations and response. According to Gartner:

“MDR must be people-focused, human-led, AI-augmented and anchored in the evidence of the successes and outcomes it delivers.”

Gartner also explains the value of this approach:

“But those services that combine automation with dynamic detection engineering and threat intelligence teams will continue to outpace an ‘automation-only’ mindset, identifying actionable countermeasures that combat the latest and most innovative threat actors.”

We believe Bitdefender MDR combines an AI-enabled SOC with round-the-clock human expertise. AI accelerates analysis and investigation, while security experts validate findings and oversee response decisions.

What Should MDR Do to Contain a Threat?

We believe an MDR provider should be ready to take agreed-upon action quickly, with clear authority and a plan to limit an attack’s spread. Alignment with your goals in this area is a key consideration for choosing the right vendor.

Gartner notes: “Assess how the MDR provider’s containment approach and incident reporting integrate with your organization. Also decide what type of actions will be performed on your behalf to align with business and compliance requirements, legal policies, and government regulations."

In our opinion, Bitdefender MDR uses pre-approved response actions to help contain threats, limit their spread, and minimize business disruption.

How Can MDR Help Reduce the Risk of an Incident?

MDR can support proactive risk and exposure reduction through threat hunting and prioritized guidance for addressing security weaknesses.

Notes Gartner: “Established MDR buyers routinely ask providers to extend their requirements beyond TDIR (threat detection and incident response) to include the proactive identification and mitigation of threat exposures.”

Bitdefender MDR leverages hundreds of millions of total covered endpoints to compile a massive amount of threat intelligence, attacker research, and threat analysis to continuously support threat hunts and update and protect customers. Our team of security experts also provides exposure insights that can help teams tackle underlying issues that might otherwise contribute to recurring risk.

Where Can You Learn More About Choosing an MDR Service?

The 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response can help security and IT leaders assess the market against their organization’s needs.

Get complimentary access to the report to inform your next MDR decision. Then explore Bitdefender MDR to learn how we believe its AI-enabled SOC and security experts can help reduce exposure, contain attacks, and extend your team’s capabilities.

Full Text:
JFrog announced completion of the first-ever Software Supply Chain Excellence Awards, recognizing the teams who have turned their software supply chain into a competitive advantage – unifying development, security and operations around a governed, automated ecosystem that delivers trusted software at scale.

The nine honorees span the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, across three categories: Unified Platform, Trusted AI Adoption, and Software Supply Chain Security.

“Agents now write, review and deploy code faster than ever, while malicious AI models, agent skills and extensions are turning up in the registries developers use daily. Increasing regulations require proof at every step – from code to runtime,” said Roie Shorer, Chief Growth Officer at JFrog. “The companies that pull ahead in the AI era will be those going beyond simply automating for speed and scale. They will be the ones who can see exactly what’s shipping and why, as they bring trust, control and adaptability to their development operations. This year’s winners didn’t just add tools; they established a single source of truth where developers, security, and compliance teams can operate using the same data and the same rules. We’re very proud of all of them and thrilled to be part of their journey.”

Software supply chains are being put under new strain as developer teams grapple with AI-era software challenges. In its 2026 Software Supply Chain Security report, JFrog identified over 900 malicious AI agent skills carrying high-impact payloads alongside 495 malicious AI models on Hugging Face and 56 malicious extensions on OpenVSX. Attackers are no longer just targeting code; they are targeting the autonomous tools that write, review, and deploy it.

This year’s JFrog Software Supply Chain Excellence Award winners are working to reduce their exposure to these emerging threats by building a system of record that governs and secures artifacts from end-to-end – mastering the AI surge with speed and trust.

THE CONVERGENCE AWARD

The Convergence Award recognizes teams that unify a fragmented software delivery workflow – bringing previously disconnected repositories, scanners and tools into a single governed system of record.

Here are the winners:

Ford (Americas): Ford Motor Company has more than 15,000 developers spread across 80-plus global plants, which previously ran on separate repository tools and scanners with no shared visibility between them. By consolidating operations into a unified ecosystem with the JFrog Platform, Ford reduced tool sprawl and turned multiple blind spots into a single pane of glass view for IT and security teams. As a result, the team now manages more than 43 million artifacts on the JFrog Platform with 99.99% uptime. The team credits the consolidation with recapturing an estimated $8 million a year in developer productivity.

SCHOTTEL Industries (EMEA): Schottel replaced fragmented artifact storage and open-source consumption with the JFrog Platform. Over six months it delivered more than 32,000 artifacts, curated over 2,300 open-source packages and automatically blocked more than 900 risky ones. Manual dependency approval processes that previously delayed developers by months were replaced by automated governance and security controls, enabling faster adoption of new technologies while helping maintain its compliance and security standards.

Rakuten Symphony (APAC): Rakuten Symphony runs 28 self-hosted JFrog Enterprise+ instances across India, Japan and Singapore, that are all connected by JFrog Federated Repositories into one collaborative environment. With JFrog Curation and JFrog Advanced Security moving controls to the point of ingestion, the company cut manual triage efforts by roughly 60% in a single month across more than 600 releases, reclaiming more than 500 engineer-hours and pre-triaging over half of its vulnerability workload automatically.

THE TRUSTED INTELLIGENCE AWARD

The Trusted Intelligence Award recognizes teams that bring enterprise-grade governance to AI and model lifecycles, helping trust extend far beyond just supporting application code.

Here are the winners:

NVIDIA (Americas): Models repositories are under enterprise identity control, with a shared curation and scanning policy,which means a downloaded model faces the same checks as a package before it reaches production.

NVIDIA brought its AI model distribution surface under a governed perimeter by applying curation, scanning, and policy enforcement directly to its model mirrors. Thousands of AI model seats are now managed inside a controlled, auditable boundary, transforming what was once an unmanaged distribution surface into a demonstration of DevGovOps operating at true enterprise scale. To get there, NVIDIA leveraged JFrog Curation and JFrog’s scanning and policy tools, piloting them on the infrastructure through which its AI models flow.

Husqvarna Group (EMEA): Husqvarna’s autonomous divisions, across forest, garden and construction equipment, had accumulated overlapping scanners with limited shared visibility into software supply chain risk. After consolidating around the JFrog Platform and introducing software package scanning and policy-based controls earlier in the software development lifecycle, builds were progressively onboarded, providing teams with greater visibility into open-source dependencies and a more consistent approach to software component governance. Husqvarna Group validated JFrog Curation and JFrog Advanced Security in a hands-on pilot ahead of full deployment, and says the centralized visibility helps streamline security and governance workflows while supporting software traceability and reporting needs associated with evolving regulatory requirements, including the EU Cyber Resilience Act and NIS2.

Singapore Airlines (APAC): Singapore Airlines moved from “trust by verification” to “trust by default.” JFrog Curation and JFrog Xray now help intercept malicious, risky or non-compliant assets before they reach a build, including AI models, MCP servers, agent skills and IDE extensions. More than 95% of AI and open-source dependencies are onboarded through curated channels prior to integration. As a result, late-stage release blocks from non-compliant dependencies are down 60-75% and the airline has full visibility of its compliance posture.

THE GUARDIAN AWARD

The Guardian Award recognizes software supply chain security operating at real enterprise scale – blocking threats before they reach production across large, highly distributed environments.

Here are the winners:

S&P Global (Americas): S&P Global’s five divisions ran on independent JFrog Artifactory clusters with no shared policy enforcement which could potentially increase risk. By putting JFrog Curation at each point of ingestion – backed by continuous rescanning – S&P addressed that gap without slowing down development teams. Critical vulnerabilities across 30 images fell by 90%, from 141 to 14. S&P reports that about 99% of malicious npm and PyPI packages are now blocked at the point of ingestion, with JFrog Curation deployed as a synchronous gate for every division and JFrog Xray continuously rescanning artifacts already in use to catch newly disclosed threats.

TSB Bank (EMEA): TSB built a continuous governance platform based on JFrog’s APIs, using GitHub Actions and Open Policy Agent, as well as a versioned Python library published to JFrog Artifactory. Automated weekly audits check configuration drift, access control, artifact integrity and artifact authenticity. In the first seven months of using the platform there were 75 governance issues, 74 of which were resolved, with 11 production repositories verified for integrity every week.

Iress (APAC): Iress put the SaaS implementation of JFrog Artifactory at the center of their 600 developer operations, and added JFrog Curation and JFrog Xray to help keep zero-day threats from entering the development environment. In just eight months, the curation initiative mitigated six critical security incidents, while eliminating 90% of reactive vulnerability triage – saving the team an estimated 13,705 engineering hours for the year.

THE SELECTION PROCESS

Award winners were selected by a cross-functional panel of JFrog leaders and industry voices who scored each submission on the breadth of its story and the strength of its metrics. The complete list of winners and full category criteria are available at jfrog.com/software-supply-chain-awards.

What you will learn

Learn which capabilities helped us achieve our 8th consecutive recognition in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™

Delinea has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM) for the eighth consecutive time.

This is our eighth time running in the Leaders Quadrant, and it comes at a moment when the identity landscape looks nothing like it did even two years ago. Enterprises are no longer just managing human and machine identities. They're managing a fast-growing population of AI agents that need access to systems, data and each other, often with no human in the loop at all. We believe this year's recognition reflects how seriously we've taken that shift.

What changed this year

Over the past twelve months, we added just-in-time runtime authorization for AI agents. In plain terms, the same granular, time-bound access controls we've long applied to human and machine identities now extend to autonomous agents operating inside enterprise environments. An agent gets exactly the access it needs, exactly when it needs it and that access goes away the moment the task is done. Decisions are made in real-time and governed by policy.

The centralized control, session monitoring and credential management features are particularly valuable, as they help enforce strong security policies while maintaining smooth operational workflows. Lead Engineer - IT Services

We think this is what will be required for authorization going forward. Access shouldn't be a standing grant that sits around waiting to be misused. It should be a decision made in the moment, based on context and revoked automatically once that moment passes. The Gartner evaluation noted our placement on the Ability to Execute axis, and we believe our shift toward dynamic, real-time authorization is a major reason why.

Why this matters to you

If you're evaluating PAM vendors right now, here's the practical takeaway: The market is being reshaped by AI agents faster than most security programs are ready for. Every agent your teams deploy is a new identity that needs governing, and static, standing access to critical infrastructure. This is exactly the kind of attack surface that gets exploited. We feel a Leader placement is just that. We see it as an independent signal from Gartner that a vendor's approach to this problem holds up in the market on both vision and execution.

Delinea Secret Server has consistently demonstrated its value as a comprehensive and scalable PAM solution. Director, IT Security and Risk Management - IT Services

For customers already on the Delinea Platform, we feel this validates the direction we've been building toward: authorization that happens at the moment of access and built on defendable policies, not before it and not as an afterthought. For prospects comparing options, it's a data point worth weighing alongside your own evaluation, not a substitute for it.

Where we believe Gartner evaluates us

Just-in-time (JIT) PAM has emerged as a core capability to counter potential rogue agentic AI. Delinea has delivered enhanced cloud-native JIT capabilities along with protocol-level ephemeral credential injection for servers, databases and Kubernetes. In practice, this means credentials are issued at the protocol level for the exact moment they're needed and never persist as standing access.

That eliminates a huge chunk of the attack surface that traditional privileged credentials create, because there's no credential sitting around to be stolen, harvested or forgotten about.

This is the same philosophy extended across three populations at once: humans (workforce), machines (workload) and now AI agents. One authorization model, applied consistently, rather than three separate systems bolted together.

Reliability isn’t an afterthought

None of this matters if the platform isn't there when you need it. We guarantee a 99.995% monthly availability SLA across our global regions, including the US, EU, Canada, Southeast Asia, the UK, Australia, and the UAE. When you're enforcing access controls at scale, and especially when those controls are making real-time decisions for AI agents, the platform making those decisions has to be dependable. We treat that as table stakes, not a bonus feature.

Customer experience as a differentiator

We've heard directly from customers that what sets Delinea apart isn't just the technology; it's how straightforward the platform is to deploy, how much support is available when questions come up, how clearly we help teams understand where they sit on the maturity curve and what to tackle next. Mapping against 70 real-world use cases isn't a marketing exercise; it's a practical tool that helps security teams figure out what "good" looks like in their specific environment, rather than guessing.

Delinea is a trusted partner of ours. We have received first-class product support and service through the years. Our organization values this vendor relationship. IT Security & Risk Management Associate - Banking

Looking ahead

Eight consecutive times as a Leader is a recognition we don't take lightly, and it's also not the finish line. The identity landscape keeps moving. AI agents are only going to multiply, attackers are already using AI to move faster and the organizations that get ahead of this will be the ones treating authorization as something dynamic and continuous rather than something you configure once and forget.

We plan to keep building in that direction by extending runtime authorization further, tightening the connection between identity context and access decisions and making sure that whatever population of identities shows up next in your environment, AI agent, human or machine, gets governed with the same rigor.

Proofpoint CEO Sumit Dhawan On ‘Market-Changing’ $6.3B Varonis Deal, IPO Goal

Full Text:
The planned acquisition of publicly traded data security vendor Varonis will enable Proofpoint partners to deliver a ‘comprehensive data security solution to their customers,’ which is primed for combating AI and agentic risk, Dhawan tells CRN.

Amid the surging adoption of AI agents, Proofpoint’s “market-changing” deal to acquire Varonis is aimed squarely at helping partners and customers to protect the data those agents can access, Proofpoint CEO Sumit Dhawan told CRN.

In an interview Friday—a day after Proofpoint’s $6.3 billion deal for publicly traded Varonis was announced—Dhawan said that the planned acquisition seeks to bring together complementary technologies for securing data and AI agents, while giving partners an even more strategic role with their customers.

[Related: 5 Things To Know On Proofpoint’s $6.3B Acquisition Of Varonis]

The deal ultimately is positioned to enable Proofpoint partners to deliver customers a broader data security platform that is primed for combating AI and agentic risk, he said.

With the combined Proofpoint-Varonis platform that is envisioned, partners will be enabled to “take a comprehensive data security solution to their customers—becoming more strategic, providing more value-added services,” Dhawan said. “And No. 2, they now can work with a single [data security] provider with a larger business.”

The combination of Varonis with Proofpoint, which was itself publicly traded until its acquisition by private equity firm Thoma Bravo in 2021, is also poised to strengthen Proofpoint’s positioning for an initial public offering, Dhawan told CRN.

“We think it’s going to be even more attractive to public investors, and our goal would be to assess that after close,” he said.

The combined company would have more than 8,000 employees with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of more than $3 billion, according to figures disclosed by the companies.

Upon completion of the combination of the two vendors, “it’s a top-five cybersecurity company with healthy growth—and more importantly, [providing] the next frontier of protection, which is data,” Dhawan said.

What follows is more of CRN’s interview with Dhawan.

What does this deal mean for the industry and the channel?

It’s a game-changing moment—just bringing together Varonis and Proofpoint makes us the [premier] data security solution in the market, especially in the world of AI. So we’re very excited.

It sounds like the ultimate plan is for this to be a combined solution from the two companies, as opposed to being Varonis operating independently of Proofpoint?

[Varonis CEO] Yaki [Faitelson] and I started the conversations a while ago. And we always compare notes on the market and whatnot. [We are] largely complementary. And earlier this year, as this whole agentic era starts shaping up, we said, look, there is clearly a next frontier on cybersecurity emerging, which is data. AI is attacking data from outside, and AI is attacking data [from] inside. And data protection needs to be done holistically. That was the vision that brought us together—to say, not just that we can have one house that will be able to serve all the portfolio. But if you’re really providing data protection, it needs to be done with machine speed. And machine-speed level of protection, in the world of AI, means integrations of our signals and control points. And that’s what our vision is. We believe we can accomplish that very, very quickly, based on just how complementary our technology stack is.

What are you hearing from your customers and your partners about how urgent of a need there is for something like this?

The whole conviction of ours is rooted on the principle that this is a board- and CEO-level priority. [When] you think about it, AI and cybersecurity, those are the two priorities for the board and CEOs. And they go hand-in-hand. Without data security, you can’t enable and adopt AI. So to me, that sort of is the grounding fact for the conviction that we have, on why data becomes the next frontier for cybersecurity—and why Proofpoint and Varonis becomes the only player that no other [vendor] can do, [providing] a full and comprehensive solution for protecting data in today’s AI-accelerated risks.

Can you say whether the combined company will operate entirely under the Proofpoint brand, or whether Varonis will still exist as a brand in some form?

We’re going to talk through it—we’re going to think that through. Those things get sorted out as we go. [Both companies have a] strong product, strong following in the customer base. So we don’t have any desired intent to make one change or the other. But it’s something we’ll figure out between now and close [of the deal].

As far as what Varonis brings in product capabilities, what specifically are you most excited about? And what do you think partners are going to be really excited about from Varonis?

What Proofpoint has built is sensing how people and AI behave when they’re interacting with data and each other—that’s our focus area. Intent-based protection, as we’ve always talked about, when people, AI and data come together. What Varonis has built is making sure that [businesses understand] where the data is and how it is getting protected based on privileges and usage. So these are a complementary set of signals. We are getting the signals on the intent and behavior, and they’re getting the signals at the data layer. Combining the two together gives you the right protection of data in today’s AI and machine-speed era. That’s the complementary nature of the solution. I’ve gotten so many positive feedback in less than 24 hours, and it’s all been about this—[they’ve been] waiting for [a vendor] who brings data security together. And Proofpoint and Varonis, because of the complementary nature of the solution, [can] become that company.

It sounds like some of the capabilities that Varonis has in certain areas are bringing something a bit different to your platform?

We already have data security solutions. We’re the market leader for DLP [data loss prevention]. We’re the market leader for insider risk solution. Those are complementary to the data security and access governance solution that Varonis brings. You combine them together, and now you can protect data at rest, and you can protect data in motion, as used by humans and AI. So think of it as data security at two different layers, working together, through a combination of signals and protection.

Are you saying how many employees the combined company will have?

Varonis has more than 2,500 employees [and] publicly we have said we have closer to 5,500 employees. As a combined company, it’s an at-scale company. We have publicly said that our ARR exiting midyear was closer to $2.5 billion. They have publicly said a little shy of $800 million exiting June. So you’re talking about a company of scale. It’s a top-five cybersecurity company with healthy growth—and more importantly, [providing] the next frontier of protection, which is data.

Envisioning the bringing together and combining of these two companies, you would say this is going to be very differentiated?

If you look at other top-five cybersecurity companies, none of those platforms were designed and built to do data protection. They’re [from] different eras of cybersecurity—endpoint, network. We become, together, the company that protects data from external threats as well as insiders. Both are being accelerated because of AI.

On the partner front, what should partners of both companies know about what this means?

Partners are excited. It happened to be that yesterday we had a European partner council, and our head of Europe was running that partner council when the news broke. And many of them said, “Hey, look, Varonis is one of our top partners. Proofpoint is one of our top partners. Together, you become maybe the No. 1 or No. 2 partner of ours going forward.” From a partner’s perspective, No. 1, most importantly, they can take a comprehensive data security solution to their customers—becoming more strategic, providing more value-added services. And No. 2, they now can work with a single provider with a larger business—which is what partners want, anyway.

Previously you talked about potentially going public at some point—probably it’s not something you would be looking at doing prior to closing this, but is there any update there?

Like you said, our focus is going to be on [closing the acquisition]. And we hope to go through the regulatory process and close the transaction as early as possible. And then we think that the combined company is quite attractive to the public investors. It’s an at-scale company, driving protection of one of the key pillars, just like any other major cybersecurity platforms are doing. We think it’s going to be even more attractive to public investors. And our goal would be to assess that after close.

Agents are something that so many businesses are grappling with, and it sounds like this combination is very much going to be tuned toward helping companies with that?

Exactly. There isn’t a day that goes by whereby we don’t read the news about risks that AI agents pose. Risks that AI agents pose doesn’t mean you have to slow down the adoption. It just means that you need to adopt AI with the right degree of security. What are these risks going after? You read all these stories. Eventually, the issue is that these AI agents go to data [systems], and the data is captured in so many different places. So enterprises need comprehensive solution that can both work on protecting the behavior of AI and protecting the data, regardless of where it exists. And that’s what Proofpoint and Varonis offers. It provides a solution that enables enterprises to go pick any agents of their choice. They’re not locked in. Go pick and enable access to any data of their choice. And in that environment, their data is protected, and they can adopt AI with speed.

There are so many different vendors coming out and saying they’re going to have some solution to this. But it sounds like part of the idea here is if you’re already protecting the data—as you and Varonis are—then you’re really in the best position to help with the agent problem, if the agent is ultimately trying to access data?

That’s 100-percent right. There is no use solving a sliver of the problem. These are interconnected problems—because eventually, agents have to access data. By protecting data, you extend that protection to protecting AI agents. So that’s why our solution in protecting agentic security—through an extension of protecting data—becomes even more powerful and real for customers.

Overall, what is the message for your partners out of this, and what is the major opportunity for them?

Firstly, I want to thank the partners that have really built the business for us. We couldn’t do it without them. And this is game-changing. It’s a market-changing, game-changing [deal], really helping customers together with partners. We can be their strategic advisors, a platform for protecting the next frontier of cybersecurity, which is data, and all driven because of AI.

Combination creates a new cybersecurity powerhouse to deliver a complete security platform that protects against AI-accelerated threats and data risks

MIAMI, FL and SUNNYVALE, CA – October 15, 2026 – Varonis Systems, Inc. (Nasdaq: VRNS) (“Varonis”), the data and AI security leader, and Proofpoint, Inc. (“Proofpoint”), a global leader in human and agent cybersecurity, today announced entrance into a definitive agreement under which Varonis will be acquired by Proofpoint, a portfolio company of Thoma Bravo, in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $6.3 billion.

Under the terms of the agreement, Varonis shareholders will receive $49.75 per share in cash. This purchase price represents a premium of 52% to Varonis’ closing stock price of $32.71 on June 22, 2026, the last full trading day prior to initial rumors about a potential sale of the Company, and a premium of 17% over Varonis’ closing stock price of $42.35 on September 1, 2026, the last trading day prior to additional media reports speculating about a potential sale of Varonis. The transaction values Varonis at approximately 53x LTM Free Cash Flow and 8.4x LTM Revenue.1

The combined company will serve more than 16,000 enterprises and millions of organizations globally, creating one of the world’s leading pure-play cybersecurity companies and establishing the industry's largest data and AI cybersecurity organization. Together, the combined company intends to deliver a unified platform that helps organizations adopt AI with confidence: finding and protecting sensitive data, controlling what people and AI can access, and stopping data loss. Following closing, Proofpoint intends to move quickly to integrate the companies’ capabilities, align go-to-market efforts, and accelerate delivery of the combined platform to customers.

“Today begins an exciting new chapter for Varonis and our customers. It’s a testament to the incredible work of the Varonis team over two decades,” said Yaki Faitelson, Varonis CEO, Co-Founder and Chairman of the Board of Directors. “Our mission is to secure AI and the data that powers it. By joining forces with Proofpoint, we can achieve this mission faster than ever.”

Faitelson continued, “This announcement follows a comprehensive evaluation led by a committee of independent members of our Board of Directors, which included extensive outreach to a range of potential strategic and financial buyers. This transaction is an excellent outcome for the company and our shareholders, representing a realization of immediate, significant, and certain value well in excess of the risk-adjusted value of delivering against our standalone plan.”

“As AI becomes embedded across the enterprise, the data it can access determines both its value and its risk. AI agents are increasingly accessing sensitive information and taking action across systems, making it critical for organizations to understand not only what data needs protecting and who can access it, but how it is actually being used,” said Sumit Dhawan, CEO of Proofpoint. “By connecting communications, identities, permissions, data, and AI, we are creating an intelligence advantage that helps customers see risk more clearly, respond faster, and defend against the next generation of AI risks. This is a defining step in Proofpoint’s evolution into a cybersecurity platform built for the future of AI.”

Transaction Details

The transaction, which has been unanimously approved by the Varonis Board of Directors, is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by Varonis shareholders and receipt of regulatory approvals. Thoma Bravo is providing committed equity financing, and has secured debt financing commitments, to fund the purchase. Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan has also agreed to make an investment into Proofpoint in connection with the transaction. Until the transaction closes, Proofpoint and Varonis will continue to operate as separate and independent companies. Upon completion of the transaction, Varonis' common stock will cease trading on the Nasdaq, and Varonis will become a private company.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Varonis will announce its financial results for the third quarter 2026 following the close of the U.S. financial markets on November 3. The news release will be available on the Investor Relations section of the company’s website. In light of the announced transaction, Varonis will not conduct an earnings conference call.

Advisors

Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC is acting as exclusive financial advisor and Paul Hastings LLP is serving as legal counsel to Varonis.

BofA Securities, Inc., Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, UBS Securities LLC, and Mizuho Securities USA LLC are serving as financial advisors, and Kirkland & Ellis LLP is serving as legal counsel to Proofpoint.

About Varonis

Varonis (Nasdaq: VRNS) secures AI and the data that powers it. The Varonis platform gives organizations automated visibility and control over their critical data wherever it lives and helps ensure safe and trustworthy AI from code to runtime. Backed by 24x7x365 managed detection and response, Varonis gives thousands of organizations worldwide the confidence to adopt AI, reduce data exposure, and stop AI-powered threats.

About Proofpoint, Inc.

Proofpoint, Inc. is a global leader in human and agent cybersecurity, securing how people, data and AI agents connect across email, cloud and collaboration tools. Proofpoint is a trusted partner to over 80 of the Fortune 100, over 14,000 large enterprises, and millions of smaller organizations in stopping threats, preventing data loss, and building resilience across people and AI workflows. Proofpoint’s collaboration, data, and AI security platform helps organizations of all sizes protect their people, defend their data, and adopt AI securely and confidently.
